title: Static analysis and SonarQube
summary: Place source analysis and imported coverage after the build, then interpret the quality gate within its limits.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: Master SonarQube, SonarLint, and SonarCloud: Ultimate Guide to Enhancing Your Code Quality

richText: Analysis in a Spring Boot build
A Boot project can use SonarQube alongside its test tools. Spring Boot does not configure SonarQube automatically.
SonarQube analyzes source code and reports findings such as suspected bugs, security issues, and duplication.
SonarScanner for Maven sends project analysis to a SonarQube server.
SonarQube for IDE reports supported rules while editing. Connected mode shares supported project settings from the server.
Coverage reports
JaCoCo records which application code executes during tests and produces a coverage report.
SonarQube imports the JaCoCo XML report. It does not run the tests or generate that coverage itself.
The build must produce the report before the scanner imports it.
Coverage says which code ran. It does not say that assertions checked every result.
Quality gates
A quality gate applies configured pass or fail conditions to an analysis.
Conditions can include new-code findings, duplication, and coverage.
An uploaded analysis is processed by the server before its quality gate result is available.
sonar.qualitygate.wait=true

example.title: Analyze the built project and wait for its gate
description: Java `17` and Maven are required. The files form a separate project rooted at `pom.xml`.
The SonarQube server already has a project with key `journal`.
The CI secret store supplies `SONAR_TOKEN`. `SONAR_HOST_URL` supplies the server URL.
The selected scanner version is compatible with the server and the CI runtime.
The commands run in order on the same project revision. The second command runs only if the first succeeds.
explanation: `verify` builds the project, runs its configured checks, and produces the configured coverage report.
The scanner reads the compiled project and the report, then sends the analysis.
The token comes from CI configuration. It does not appear in the command or repository.
The invocation waits for the server’s gate result. Network failure or a gate timeout can also fail the invocation.

richText: Interpreting results
A passing gate means the configured conditions passed. It does not prove every application behavior.
A finding may require a code change or a documented suppression after review.
Generated-code exclusions follow project policy. Excluding application code hides its results too.
The deployment lessons next use the built artifact. Analysis and tests do not verify the target host configuration.
